low_area_control.author: llm
low_area_control.lesson: For area-min CORDIC specs, iterative family with data_width=16, n_iter=12, truncation wins (267 LUTs+FFs, 10.5 acc bits, 13.2 MSPS). L3/L4 have no recorded rows for this design class, so back_annotate returns no_measured_data and reexplore is refused; finalize directly after L2.

note/bursty_offload.author: llm
note/bursty_offload.lesson: For bursty specs (bursts of 8, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 <= 0.4 us), pipelined_m wins: dw=15, n_iter=14, m=7 (855 LUTs+FFs est, 10.6 acc bits, 59.6 MSPS, simulated p99 0.233 us). L1 analytic p99 bound was optimistic (~0.17 vs simulated 0.233) but still passed. pipelined_m reached the front here, unlike prior campaigns. No L3/L4 measured rows; back_annotate no_measured_data, finalize directly.

note/dds_250msps.author: llm
note/dds_250msps.lesson: For the 250 MSPS DDS spec (min LUTs, err <= 2^-13), plain pipelined family won: dw=19, n_iter=15, no guards, round (935 LUTs est, 13.2 acc bits, 264 MSPS, 2^-13.18). Notable: pipelined reached the front here, unlike prior campaigns where it never did; pipelined_m and unrolled_k did not beat it on LUTs at this throughput. L2 DDS sim: SFDR 100.5 dBc, SNR 88.3 dB. No L3/L4 measured rows; back_annotate no_measured_data, finalize directly.

note/multiaxis_control.author: llm
note/multiaxis_control.lesson: For the 16-axis control spec (32 req/tick, p99 <= 0.44us, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m dw=18, n_iter=16, no guards, round, m=4 won: 1236 LUTs+FFs est, 13 acc bits, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.378us. Key lesson: the m=5/dw=15 designs (1070-1145 LUTs) looked cheaper at L1 (analytic p99 0.434) but SimPy gave 0.4465 -> failed the 0.44us bound by 1.5%; L2 flipped the winner to the m=4/dw=18 design. The L1 analytic p99 bound is optimistic for bursty 32-request ticks; keep >= ~5% margin on t

bursty_offload.author: llm
bursty_offload.lesson: For bursty p99-latency CORDIC specs (bursts of 8, 2 req/us, p99 <= 0.4 us, err <= 2^-10, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m with m=4, data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=2, rounding=round wins (est 813 luts+ffs, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.135 us). Single-iteration iterative designs are too slow to drain 8-request bursts within p99; pipelined_m m=4 was the area/latency sweet spot. No L3/L4 measurements recorded for this design.

low_area_control.author: llm
low_area_control.lesson: For area-min CORDIC specs (>=1 MSPS, err <= 2^-10), iterative family with data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=1, rounding=round wins (est 251 luts+ffs, measured 216 LUTs/107 FFs/150.7 MHz). Cost model underestimates LUTs by ~19% and FFs by ~11% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx; Fmax underestimated by ~10%. Pipelined variants too area-hungry for this class.

multiaxis_control.author: llm
multiaxis_control.lesson: For 32-request-per-tick CORDIC specs (32 req/us, p99 batch <= 0.44us, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m m=4, data_width=16, n_iter=14, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=2, rounding=round wins (est 1137 luts+ffs, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.378us). m=4 suffices even for 32-deep bursts at 1us ticks because throughput 97.8 MSPS >> 32 MSPS; the p99 window is dominated by pipeline drain, not throughput. No L3/L4 measurements recorded; L5 back_annotate returned no_measured_data.

note/dds_250msps.author: llm
note/dds_250msps.lesson: For high-rate (>=250 MSPS, 1 sample/clock) CORDIC specs with err <= 2^-13, min LUTs: pipelined (m=1) family with data_width=18, n_iter=15, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=0, rounding=round wins (est 920 LUTs, 953 FFs, 264 MSPS, err 2^-13.17). The sweet spot is data_width 18, n_iter 15; angle_guard 2 with rounding=round is cheapest. No L3/L4 measurements recorded for this design; L5 back_annotate returned no_measured_data.

bursty_offload.author: llm
bursty_offload.lesson: For bursty Poisson 8-req bursts (2 req/us, p99<=0.4us) with min LUTs+FFs: pipelined_m dominated the front (m=4..7, dw=15..20, n_iter=12..13); winner pipelined_m dw=15/n_iter=12/m=7 (est 816 LUTs+FFs, 10.1 bits, sim p99 0.233us). L1 analytic p99 bounds under-predicted simulated p99 by ~1.4-1.5x (0.168->0.233) but all top-5 still passed. No recorded L3/L4 rows for pipelined_m designs, so no measured confirmation.

low_area_control.author: llm
low_area_control.lesson: For area-min CORDIC specs, iterative dw=15/n_iter=12 wins; M1 cost model under-predicts LUTs ~19% and FFs ~11% vs yosys+nextpnr measured (216 LUT/107 FF vs est 159/92). No winner change at L5.

note/dds_250msps.author: llm
note/dds_250msps.lesson: For 1-sample/clock DDS specs (>=250 MSPS, min LUTs): only plain pipelined reached the front (dw 15..18, n_iter 14..16); pipelined_m (m=2..4, dw 14..17, n_iter 12..13) had 0 feasible in that box, and iterative can't hit 1/cycle. Winner pipelined dw=18/n_iter=15/angle_guard=2/frac_guard=1/trunc (est 949 LUTs, 13.1 bits, 264 MSPS). L2 DDS sim: SFDR 98.2 dBc, SNR 87.5 dB. No recorded L3/L4 rows for pipelined designs, so no measured confirmation.

note/multiaxis_control.author: llm
note/multiaxis_control.lesson: For 32-req-per-tick batch specs (p99<=0.44us, min LUTs+FFs): pipelined_m m=2 dominated the front (dw 19..20, n_iter 14..16); winner pipelined_m dw=19/n_iter=14/m=2/trunc (est 1417 LUTs+FFs, 12.4 bits, 164 MSPS, sim p99 0.243us). L1 analytic p99 under-predicted sim by ~2.5% (0.237->0.243), much less than the ~1.4-1.5x on the bursty spec. No recorded L3/L4 rows for pipelined_m, so no measured confirmation.
